summary: Hermann Hupfeld worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Marburg (~1813–1817) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1821–1824), later holding posts at Marburg (~1825–1843) and Halle-Wittenberg (~1843–1866).

Hermann Jacobi was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber at Humboldt University of Berlin and Johann Gildemeister at the University of Bonn. He held professorships at Münster (1876–1885), Kiel (1885), and Bonn (1889–1922).

Hermann Kulke worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Hermann Goetz, at the University of Madras, University of Freiburg, and Heidelberg University. His main appointments included Heidelberg University (1967–1988) and Kiel University (1988–2003).

Hermann Oldenberg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held professorships at Berlin (1878), Kiel University (1889–1908), and Göttingen (1908).

Hermann Olshausen specialized in religious studies. He studied at Kiel University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Berlin (~1820–1821), the University of Königsberg (1827–1834), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1834–1839).

Hermann Osthoff was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Bonn under Hermann Usener, and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He held posts at Friedrichsgymnasium Kassel, the University of Leipzig (~1875–1877), and Heidelberg University (1877).

Hermann Sauppe worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He earned his doctorate under Gottfried Hermann at the University of Leipzig. He held posts at Zurich (1833), Zentralbibliothek Zürich (1837), Weimar (1845), and the University of Göttingen (1855).
Hermann Schlagintweit studied at the University of Munich (~1845–1848). He later held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1852 to 1854.

Hermann Usener was a religious studies scholar. He studied at Munich, Heidelberg, Göttingen, and Bonn. His career included posts at the University of Bern (~1861–1863), University of Greifswald (~1863–1866), and University of Bonn (~1866–1905).

Hermann Wilhelm Ebel specialized in linguistics, studying under August Boeckh, August Friedrich Pott, and doctoral supervisor Franz Bopp. He held posts at Beheim-Schwarzbach'sche Realschule, Gymnasium Schneidemühl, and as chair of comparative philology at Humboldt University of Berlin (1872).

Hew McLeod specialized in Indology, religious studies, and history. He studied at Nelson College, the University of Otago, and SOAS University of London, and later held a post at the University of Otago (~1971–1997).

Heymann Steinthal was a scholar of linguistics and philosophy who studied under August Boeckh at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1843–1847). He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1850–1899) and the Hochschule für die Wissenschaft des Judentums (~1872–1899).
Hideaki Kimura is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He also held a researcher post at Taisho University, attested in 1995.

Hideaki Nakatani is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He studied at Kyoto University and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Gadjin Nagao and Yutaka Ochihara. He was attested as a professor at Kobe Gakuin University in 2003.
Hidehiko Kurita works in religious studies and Japanology. He completed his PhD at Tohoku University and served as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University, attested in 2020.
Hideki Kiyoshima is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Delhi and held a lecturer post at Kindai University, attested in 1989.
Hidemasa Nagata was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1953 to 1961 and held a post there from around 1967 to 1997.

Hidenaka Tanaka was a linguist who studied under Raphael von Koeber at the University of Tokyo, Oxford, and Kyoto University. He taught at the University of Tokyo, Kyoto University (1920; 1931–1946), and Kyoto Women's University (~1950–1974).

Hidenori Kitagawa worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, studying under Hakuju Ui. He was a Rockefeller Foundation fellow (1952–1953) and served as a professor at Nagoya University (attested 1968–1969).

Hidenori S. Sakuma works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg. He held professorships at Shitennoji University (attested 1991–1998) and University of Tsukuba (attested 2003–2011).
